title: A KES 45,000 write-off for water-damaged Safi Laundry Detergent 1Kg must pass through Inventory, Finance and Records
description: Nakuru Distribution Centre identifies water-damaged cartons of Safi Laundry Detergent 1Kg valued at approximately KES 45,000. The stock is segregated, and the write-off must be approved and recorded before it leaves the books.
businessContext: This chain runs from the physical warehouse finding, through the Inventory Manager's accounting treatment, to the financial approval matrix, and into the retained record.

events.event: Nakuru Distribution Centre identifies water-damaged cartons of Safi Laundry Detergent 1Kg valued at KES 45,000.
The stock is segregated, labelled and held from sale.
The Inventory Manager proposes a write-off for the damaged quantity.
Nancy Wairimu Ndungu (Warehouse Manager) approves the write-off under FIN-POL-002.
The count evidence, approval and adjustment are retained under GEN-POL-001.

expectedOutcome: The KES 45,000 write-off requires the Inventory Manager's sign-off under INV-POL-001 plus Nancy Wairimu Ndungu (Warehouse Manager)'s approval under the FIN-POL-002 matrix for this amount; the warehouse cannot post the adjustment unilaterally, and the full evidence trail is retained under GEN-POL-001.
relevantFacts: Safi Laundry Detergent 1Kg (PRD-021) at Nakuru Distribution Centre (WH-NKR-001) has an estimated damaged-stock value of KES 45,000.
WH-POL-001: 'The warehouse may not create an unexplained adjustment.'
INV-POL-001: 'Write-offs for damage, expiry, loss or obsolescence require the Inventory Manager and the approval level in FIN-POL-002.'
requiredReasoning: Identify the physical control step (segregation) versus the accounting step (write-off).
Resolve the FIN-POL-002 approver for this amount.
Identify what must be retained once the write-off is approved.
